text:
I haven't run anything yet. I need four answers first, because setup gives this laptop a forge token and changes how it uses memory.

**Questions**

1. **Memory.** I propose 2 GiB while you're on battery or working, and 16 GiB (half of your 32 GB) only when plugged in. On battery, should CI stop taking jobs entirely? I'd recommend yes, since you said it shouldn't run while you work unplugged.
2. **Token.** Setup stores acme-dev's `gh` token on this laptop so it can register runners for acme/webapp. Anything that runs on this laptop could then act with that token, so it's a real trust decision. Is that OK? Runner registration also needs admin rights on the repo, so I'll first check that acme-dev has them. That check is read-only.
3. **Device name.** I'll use the hostname, lowercased, unless you want something else.
4. **Workflow edits.** Jobs only reach this laptop after their `runs-on` changes. I'll show you a report of the changes first. I won't write, commit or push anything without your yes.

Once you answer, I'd run:

```sh
# 1. Read-only: confirm acme-dev is admin on the repo
gh api repos/acme/webapp --jq '.permissions'

# 2. Install the binary without setup (sudo puts it in /usr/local/bin)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baney75/tentmaker/main/scripts/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- --no-setup

# 3. Set up with the budget you approve (no prompts)
sudo tentmaker setup --yes --json --repo acme/webapp \
  --memory 2GiB --boost-memory 16GiB --on-battery off

# 4. Verify and check the budget
sudo tentmaker doctor --json
tentmaker budget --json
tentmaker status --json
```

Two things to check in the doctor output. Tart needs macOS 26 or newer, and this Mac runs 27.2, so that's fine. Guards also pause CI when less than 20 GiB of disk is free, and a macOS VM image takes a lot of space, so check free disk early.

Repo is private, so `--allow-public` isn't needed. Fork pull requests still never run on this laptop.

After setup, I'd report the `runs-on` edits (`tentmaker migrate ~/path/to/webapp --platform macos --json`) and wait for your yes before changing any file.
